sections.title: Budget: measurable hard caps (the REAL guards — always honored)
comment: These are the ceilings the conductor can actually COUNT, so they are what truly stops a
runaway. They are tallied from the conductor's OWN tool calls + item/retry counts and logged
to loop.jsonl. The token estimates below CANNOT be enforced precisely — do not rely on them.
sections.example_title: Budget: measurable hard caps (the real guards)

sections.title: Budget: token estimates (BEST-EFFORT soft-stops — NOT enforceable)
comment: The executor CANNOT read its own exact token count, so these are ESTIMATES only. They make the
loop pause when work is CLEARLY over budget; they are not a precise gate and must never be
presented as one. The measurable caps above are the hard guards. (Read these as "_est".)
sections.example_title: Budget: token estimates (best-effort soft-stops, not enforceable)

sections.title: Verification (local-first; see .claude/context/local-dev.md)
comment: EXECUTION-CRITICAL: if any of these is left as <command>, /orchestrate HARD-STOPS at
the preamble (downgrading autonomy is not enough — the loop can't pass a verify gate).

keys.name: autonomy
doc: per-feature | per-milestone | unattended
per-feature   = pause after every item (max oversight)
per-milestone = pause at milestone boundaries (default)
unattended    = no discretionary pauses (hard-stops still fire)
pause at milestone boundaries

keys.name: max_retries_per_item
doc: caps three within-item loops INDEPENDENTLY (each gets its own
counter): verify retries, code-review re-dispatches, and PARTIAL
split re-dispatches. Worst case is bounded by max_tool_calls_per_item.
within-item verify retries before `blocked`

keys.name: max_consecutive_failures
doc: circuit breaker: consecutive `blocked` items (no `done` between) -> hard-stop
counts FAILED ITEMS, not within-item retries
consecutive blocked items -> hard-stop

keys.name: max_items_per_run
doc: HARD global ceiling on items attempted in one run
hard global ceiling on items per run

keys.name: max_tool_calls_per_item
doc: HARD per-item ceiling on the conductor's OWN tool calls
(Agent dispatches, code-review, security-review, verify, git,
reads/writes). This is the backstop that actually bounds a single
item — the token caps below can't. Breach -> budget_halted.
Raise it for items that fan out to many engineers; it's a runaway
backstop, not a tuning target.
hard per-item ceiling on the conductor's own tool calls

keys.name: max_tool_calls_per_run
doc: HARD global ceiling on the conductor's own tool calls across the run
hard global ceiling across the run

keys.name: token_budget_per_item
doc: best-effort estimate; pause when clearly exceeded

keys.name: total_token_budget_per_run
doc: best-effort global estimate

keys.name: verify_tests
doc: e.g. "pnpm test" — must exit 0 AND collect >0 tests
vitest across the workspace; must exit 0 AND collect >0 tests

keys.name: verify_run
doc: how to boot the app locally for the per-item runtime assertion
e.g. "pnpm dev" + a preview assertion on the item's demo target
boot web (5173) + admin (5174) + API (3001), then run the
verify-run harness in local-dev.md: poll the item's demo-target
route until it responds, curl -sf http://localhost:3001/api/health,
kill the dev server, exit with the health check's code

keys.name: security_review
doc: sensitive (default) | every_item | off
sensitive  = run the security-reviewer agent on any item whose
design touches auth, payments, file uploads, or
user-supplied input
every_item = run it on every item
off        = never run it in the loop (NOT recommended for an
unattended run that ships user-facing features)
Any Critical/High finding -> hard-stop (security_blocked); the item
does NOT reach `done` until the findings are resolved, or the USER
records a securityWaiver on the item (justification required —
only the user can grant it, at the hard-stop or unblock step).
run security-reviewer on auth / payments / uploads / user-input items

keys.name: db_local
doc: sqlite | postgres. The local engine must match PRODUCTION (DEC-8):
sqlite only if prod is SQLite or libSQL; otherwise postgres, in-process
first (PGlite / embedded-postgres), then a container. Set it explicitly.
No matching engine available: doctor error, level capped at L1.
See .claude/context/local-dev-rules.md
in-process Postgres (PGlite); prod is Postgres 16 on RDS

keys.name: db_ephemeral
doc: EXECUTION-CRITICAL (hard-stop if left as <command>): how to spin
a throwaway per-item DB + how the DATABASE_URL override reaches the
verify subprocess (document the exact commands in local-dev.md)
postgres: CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE <seeded> (seconds), or a
disposable container
sqlite (only if prod is SQLite): copy/delete a temp .db file
CREATE DATABASE taskflow_item_$ID TEMPLATE taskflow_seeded; verify subprocess
gets DATABASE_URL pointing at it; drop it after verify (see local-dev.md,
Ephemeral Per-Item DB)

keys.name: git_strategy
doc: the only V1 strategy
after_doc: The conductor branches each item off main, merges to LOCAL main on verify-pass, and NEVER pushes.

doc: the only V1 strategy; conductor never pushes

keys.name: infra_gated_behind_local
doc: deploy/IaC milestones won't start until the app runs locally
infra-touching items always force a checkpoint regardless of autonomy
CDK milestones wait until the app runs locally; infra items force a checkpoint

keys.name: enforce_engineer_git_hook
doc: documents whether you keep the shipped PreToolUse hook
(.claude/hooks/guard-git.sh) wired. NOTHING READS THIS VALUE: the hook
is on or off by its entry in .claude/settings.json, not by this flag.
HONEST SCOPE: the hook blocks only universally-forbidden shared-history
ops (push, rebase, non-feat force-delete, shared hard-reset) for EVERY
actor; it cannot tell an engineer's `git commit` from the conductor's.
The "engineers are git-read-only" boundary itself is protocol convention
(engineer-protocol §8). The hook FAILS OPEN (allows) when python3 is
missing or the command cannot be parsed, until the v2 guards (Phase 2)
replace it. If false, you accept the residual risk with no hook backstop.
keep guard-git.sh wired: blocks push/rebase/shared hard-reset for every
actor, fails open without python3 (engineer git-read-only is convention)
